package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp update was maliciously modified as part of a sophisticated software supply chain attack. Attackers compromised the build environment of an upstream vendor (Trading Technologies), inserted a trojan into their software, which was then consumed by 3CX, resulting in the distribution of a tampered 3CXDesktopApp update containing malware to customers. This chained compromise enabled widespread malware deployment through a trusted software channel.

malicious_snippets.code_language: Unknown (likely C++ or JavaScript, depending on 3CXDesktopApp's tech stack; report suggests DLL and JavaScript components)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation or update, the code is executed as part of the legitimate 3CXDesktopApp process, loads a malicious DLL via sideloading, establishes outbound network connections to attacker-controlled domains, and exfiltrates sensitive data or downloads additional payloads, resulting in remote attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is present only in tampered update packages and causes the trusted 3CXDesktopApp to initiate unauthorized network communications to external, attacker-controlled infrastructure, which is not expected in legitimate updates. The use of DLL sideloading and post-update network beaconing is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software updates should only contain vendor-approved code and should not introduce new network connections to unknown domains or load unauthorized DLLs. The presence of code that initiates external communications or loads untrusted modules violates standard software integrity and security practices.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate applications may contact official update servers or check for new versions, but should not connect to unrecognized domains or load DLLs from unexpected locations. Any network activity should be to known, vendor-controlled endpoints.
key_indicators: Presence of unauthorized DLLs or code in the update package
Network connections from 3CXDesktopApp to non-standard, attacker-controlled domains after update
Execution of new code not present in previous versions
DLL sideloading behavior within the 3CXDesktopApp process

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The build pipeline was compromised to insert unauthorized code into software artifacts, resulting in downstream software (including 3CXDesktopApp) being trojanized without the knowledge of the vendor or users. This is a hallmark of a supply chain attack.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build pipelines should be secure and only produce software from trusted, reviewed source code. Any modification of build artifacts by unauthorized code is a severe violation of software supply chain integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build scripts are common in software development, but they should not introduce unreviewed or unauthorized code into distributed binaries. All changes should be traceable and approved.

Compare updated binaries and DLLs against known-good versions to detect unauthorized modifications. Audit build pipelines and supply chain dependencies for unauthorized changes or tampering.
